result:
`browser.start` now accepts `edge` (or `msedge`) and launches an isolated Microsoft Edge pointed at the proxy. I haven't run the tests, as instructed.

- **`mitmproxy/addons/browser.py`:**
  - Added `launch_edge()`. It looks for Edge on macOS, on Windows (both Program Files paths), and on Linux (`microsoft-edge`, `-stable`, `-beta`, `-dev`, `msedge`). It falls back to the `com.microsoft.Edge` flatpak. If nothing is found, it logs the same "platform is not supported" alert as the other browsers.
  - Edge is Chromium-based and takes the same flags as Chrome, so I moved the shared launch code into a private `_launch_chromium(cmd)` helper. It creates a temporary profile directory and sets `--proxy-server` plus the first-run and extension flags. `launch_chrome()` and `launch_edge()` both use it.
- **`test/mitmproxy/addons/test_browser.py`:** Added two tests. One checks that Edge launches with `--proxy-server=127.0.0.1:8080`. The other checks the "not found" message.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`:** Added an entry under Unreleased.

I didn't run `individual_coverage`, since no new source files were added.
